sections.h2: How does Findlay's housing market work for a seller?
sections.html:
Findlay sells to people tied to the local payroll. The city is the seat of Hancock County and the second-largest in Northwest Ohio, roughly 40 miles south of Toledo, and its housing demand follows hiring at the refinery-era headquarters, appliance plant and hospital more than the season.

The Blanchard River cuts across town from east to west. The settlement began as Fort Findlay, a stockade raised in the War of 1812, and the first lots were platted in 1821. Oil and gas drilling in the 1880s lifted the population from 4,633 in 1880 to 18,553 by 1890, which is why blocks near downtown hold so much housing from that period. Subdivisions fill the rest of the 19.64 square miles of land.

Most owners choose among an agent listing, a sale by owner and a direct purchase by an investor. The sections below cover the Findlay details that change the numbers on each.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Findlay homes?
sections.html:
Findlay prices sit well under the Columbus and Cleveland suburbs. Nearly four in ten households rent, which keeps a steady pool of landlords and tenants-turned-buyers in the market.

sections.h2: How does the Blanchard River affect selling a Findlay house?
sections.html:
Flood exposure is the first property-specific question Findlay buyers and lenders raise. The river crested at 18.46 feet in 2007, causing around $100 million in damage and coming close to the 1913 record.

The city floodplain page lays out what an owner should know:

  • The city participates in the National Flood Insurance Program, so any parcel can be insured through it or a private carrier.
  • Grading, new construction and alterations inside a Special Flood Hazard Area need a Flood Development Permit before work begins.
  • Structural damage in that area, from flood, fire, wind or anything else, goes to the Zoning Department for a damage assessment.
  • The Hancock County Auditor maps show whether a given parcel sits in the hazard area, and zoning staff will help read them.

After the first phase of river benching, the city sent FEMA a Letter of Map Revision proposing to remove or shrink flood zones over a significant amount of land, and the flood information page links a parcel list. Check whether your lot appears there before you pick an asking price, because a revised map can change a buyer's insurance bill.

Weather also tests the structure. Findlay gets roughly 37.7 inches of precipitation and 23.8 inches of snow in a typical year, and the record low is minus 21, so inspectors and buyers look closely at roofs, gutters, sump pumps and basement walls.

sections.h2: Which Findlay employers and roads feed buyer demand?
sections.html:
Few cities Findlay's size depend on such a short list of big names. Marathon Petroleum has its headquarters downtown, Whirlpool operates what is considered the world's largest dishwasher plant by output, and Lowe's, Kohl's, Best Buy and Campbell Soup run distribution centers here. Cooper Tire, founded in Findlay in 1914, came under Goodyear in 2021.

Top local employers in the city's 2024 financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia:

  • Blanchard Valley Regional Health Center, 3,165 employees
  • Marathon Petroleum, 2,159
  • Whirlpool, 1,930
  • Goodyear, 895
  • Findlay City Schools, 865
  • The University of Findlay, 548

Interstate 75 crosses the city, US 68 ends here, and US 224 plus Ohio routes 12, 15, 37 and 568 all pass through. The University of Findlay enrolls over 4,100 students and Owens Community College adds more, so a rental or starter home near campus has its own buyer group. Public school students attend Findlay City Schools, and Findlay High School covers grades 9 to 12.

sections.h2: What does Hancock County charge to transfer a Findlay deed?
sections.html:
The county Auditor takes $3 for every thousand dollars conveyed, rounded to the nearest ten cents, and adds $0.50 per parcel. Some transfers are exempt from the conveyance portion.

According to the Hancock County property transfer page, the Auditor needs a DTE 100 statement of value (or a DTE 100(EX) when an exemption applies) and a notarized deed whose legal description is exact. Make checks payable to the Hancock County Auditor. The Real Estate Division is in room 21 on the second floor of the courthouse at 300 S. Main Street, and its phone is 419-424-7015.

Recording is a separate step with the county recorder. The recorder's fee schedule lists $39 for a document's first two pages and $8 per added page since January 2025. The seller signs the deed before a notary or another officer named in ORC 5301.01.

sections.h2: What else shapes a Findlay neighborhood besides the river?
sections.html:
Findlay brands itself Flag City, USA, and the calendar gives buyers a feel for daily life: Boogie on the Block in June, the Flag City BalloonFest in August, then Oktoberfest and a Halloween parade in the fall, with the Hancock County Fair as an anchor.

The Findlay Reservoir No. 2, at roughly 5 billion gallons, is the largest above-ground reservoir in Ohio. Riverside Park holds the weir on the Blanchard, the Findlay-Hancock County Public Library has served the city since 1888, and the University of Findlay runs a 152-acre farm for its equestrian and pre-veterinary students. Findlay Airport lies about two nautical miles south-southwest of the central business district.

For a seller, these details help a listing explain itself: a short drive to a park, a school or a plant gate is what a Findlay buyer usually asks about first.

sections.h2: What must a Findlay seller hand the buyer?
sections.html:
Covered sellers give the buyer the state property disclosure form (ORC 5302.30). A buyer who gets it only after signing a contract has three business days after receipt to cancel.

Estate representatives, heirs who never lived in the home and transfers inside a family are among the listed exceptions, which matters in a city with so many long-held family houses.

sections.h2: What are the practical ways to sell a Findlay house?
sections.html:
Picking a route depends on how much repair work the house needs and how soon you need the money.

  • Agent listing: reaches the most buyers, and showings and lender timing shape the closing date.
  • Sale by owner: skips the commission, and you prepare the disclosure form, DTE 100 and deed yourself.
  • Cash purchase: the buyer takes the house as it stands and you choose the closing date, usually at a lower price.
  • Family or neighbor sale: easier talks, with the same Auditor paperwork unless an exemption fits.

Two written offers, compared by what you net after fees, tax proration and any payoff, show which route pays best.

faqs.q: Does a Findlay home near the river sell for less?
faqs.a: It can, since flood insurance adds a cost for the buyer. Look up the parcel on the Hancock County Auditor maps, ask Zoning about the proposed map revision, and gather elevation or insurance records before listing.

faqs.q: What is the Hancock County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: It is $3 per thousand dollars conveyed plus $0.50 per parcel. Recording adds $39 for the first two pages and $8 per extra page, and the Real Estate Division can give an exact total for your deed.

faqs.q: Do I have to repair a Findlay house before selling?
faqs.a: No Ohio rule demands repairs before a sale. A covered seller does have to disclose known problems on the state form, and mortgage buyers often ask for fixes after inspection, while as-is buyers price the work in.

faqs.q: Where is the deed filed once a Findlay sale closes?
faqs.a: The Hancock County Recorder in Findlay files it after the Auditor endorses the conveyance. An unrecorded deed is treated as fraudulent against a later buyer who had no notice of it (ORC 5301.25), so closing agents file quickly.

faqs.q: Who buys houses in Findlay besides families?
faqs.a: Investors and landlords buy here because about 40 percent of households rent and the median rent is $975. Employees of the plants and the hospital, plus University of Findlay staff, also shop for houses in town.
